item.title: Chinese scientists develop rice's full-lifecycle cell atlas
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Chinese scientists develop rice's full-lifecycle cell atlas HAIKOU, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- Chinese researchers have developed the world's first three-dimensional spatiotemporal cell atlas that tracks the entire growth lifecycle of rice. The landmark findings, published online Tuesday in the international journal Cell, resolve long-standing bottlenecks in observing and understanding how rice cells grow, divide and coordinate to shape the crop. Led by Yazhouwan National Laboratory based in south China's Hainan Province, a consortium of 12 research institutions, including Chinese biotech firm BGI-Research and Huazhong Agricultural University, built a 3D spatiotemporal cell atlas covering rice's entire journey, from seed germination to flowering and grain filling. The resource supports future efforts to improve grain quality, according to the team. Using the widely cultivated japonica rice variety Zhonghua 11 as the research subject, the scientists integrated self-developed spatial omics, single-cell omics and high-throughput sequencing technologies to build a comprehensive rice cell atlas. Covering 10 types of rice organs and tissues and 61 continuous developmental stages, the atlas is built on more than 850,000 high-quality single-nucleus datasets and over 340,000 spatial data units. The team precisely identified and annotated 119 cell types and 133 cell subtypes, successfully matching each cell's molecular features with its spatial location and dynamic changes across growth stages. The high-resolution atlas enables researchers to visually and systematically observe how different rice cells collaborate and self-organize to form a complete plant, offering an unprecedented tool for decoding rice developmental mechanisms. To further support global rice research, the team also developed a single-cell foundation model for rice, which enables efficient identification, comparison and reuse of massive omics data, providing vital technical support for identifying key functional genes and advancing innovative, precision rice breeding research. item.title: Group of Friends of Global Governance calls for respect for int'l rule of law
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Group of Friends of Global Governance calls for respect for int'l rule of law UNITED NATIONS, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- The Group of Friends of Global Governance on Wednesday called for respect for the international rule of law. The rule of law is a hallmark of the progress of human civilization, providing an essential legal safeguard around which societies are built and international order is shaped, the group said in a joint statement delivered by China on its behalf at the UN General Assembly. Noting that the international order is again facing turbulence and instability, the group said the rule of law at the international level is under serious strain, risking undermining global peace and security. "The foundation of the international rule of law lies in faithful adherence to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter," said the statement. "All parties should defend the authority and integrity of international law and jointly uphold the international order based on international law." The group stressed that all states enjoy equal rights and bear equal obligations under international law, firmly rejecting double standards and the selective application of international rules. It urged countries to refrain from unilateral economic, financial and trade measures inconsistent with international law and the UN Charter and that impede economic and social development, particularly in developing countries. It also called on parties to settle disputes through peaceful means of their own choice and opposed the threat or use of force in international relations. International law must keep pace with rapidly advancing technology and provide guidance for its governance, it said, urging all parties to strengthen global governance in emerging areas such as cyberspace, outer space, the deep sea, the polar regions and artificial intelligence, preventing them from becoming new arenas for rivalry and instead making them avenues for cooperation. The group stands ready to work with all parties to uphold the UN-centered international system and an international order based on international law, while advancing the rule of law, fairness and justice at the national and international levels, said the statement. item.title: Chinese innovation and engineering take center stage at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Chinese innovation and engineering take center stage at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games The Cambodian Asian Games delegation is outfitted with custom-made uniforms from 361 Degrees. (Photo from the official account of 361 Degrees on WeChat) The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games came to a close on Oct. 4 after a two-week competition, with China topping the gold medal table for the 12th consecutive edition. From the opening ceremony's grand staging to athletes' uniforms and competition venues, Chinese technological innovation and design excellence played a pivotal role across the Games. Several Chinese brands and their engineering delivered integrated solutions that highlighted the strength and adaptability of China's manufacturing and creative industries. Following the lighting of the main cauldron, the opening ceremony featured a sequence of choreographed performances and visual spectacles. The stage engineering, design, and development of the main cauldron tower, digital content, and on-site implementation for the grand ceremony were all carried out by a project team from Dafeng Industry, a Chinese provider of integrated solutions for cultural, sports, and tourism industries based in east China's Zhejiang province. Working closely with organizers, the team managed everything from creative direction and production to system integration and operational management. Powered by proprietary Chinese software and hardware, the unified platform guaranteed seamless coordination of all critical ceremony elements. Nagoya's coastal location presented significant environmental challenges. Prone to typhoons and seasonal downpours, the region requires outdoor structures to meet rigorous standards for wind resistance, seismic safety, waterproofing, and structural redundancy. "The real challenge wasn't any single piece of equipment; it was integrating dozens of interdependent subsystems. Even a millisecond-level delay in lighting, stage machinery, projection, or audio could cascade into a major disruption," said Xu Huiwen, technical director of the opening and closing ceremonies of the 20th Asian Games and technical director of the stage design institute of Dafeng Industry. Multiple challenges of the project have been resolved through a two-site coordination model. A team in Zhejiang province's Hangzhou was responsible for refining the technical plans and developing digital content. Using digital twin technology, it simulated wind patterns and lighting effects around the main cauldron tower at the Nagoya site, assessed the potential risks posed by typhoons and heavy rain in advance, and carried out coordinated testing of stage-design subsystems as well as cross-border reviews online. Meanwhile, the company's smart manufacturing base in Yuyao, Ningbo, Zhejiang, was responsible for equipment manufacturing. The entire main cauldron tower was produced there, underwent multiple rounds of stress tests and extreme-condition testing, and was packed and shipped to Japan in August 2026. By completing extensive debugging and testing in China ahead of time, the team significantly reduced the workload of on-site construction in Japan. The main cauldron of the 20th Asian Games is manufactured in Yuyao, Ningbo, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Ni Yanqiang) This is not the first time the team has worked on an international multi-sport event. Dafeng Industry's technical solutions have previously been used at major events including the Jakarta Asian Games, Beijing Winter Olympics and Hangzhou Asian Games. The company also provided stage support for the G20 Hangzhou Summit, building extensive experience in delivering large-scale engineering projects across the entire process and across national borders. The company is now continuing to explore ways to take its equipment, creative solutions, and technical standards overseas. Its technologies and services have been deployed in more than 100 countries and regions around the world. Around the Asian Games venues, volunteer Makino moved through the stands in a forest-green uniform, helping guide spectators. "It's incredibly lightweight and breathable. It wicks moisture efficiently and dries quickly, which makes a huge difference in humid conditions," Makino said. The uniform is made by Chinese sportswear brand 361 Degrees. As an official partner of the Games, 361 Degrees has provided official sportswear for torchbearers, torch relay runners, volunteers, and technical officials. The garments utilize advanced quick-dry, ultra-light fabrics engineered to withstand repeated laundering without losing performance. Each cut was optimized through biomechanical modeling and motion-simulation studies, ensuring athletes and staff remain agile and comfortable during prolonged outdoor activity. Design details also feature in the uniforms of several national and regional delegations. The uniform for the Cambodian delegation draws inspiration from the architectural contours of Angkor Wat, while the uniform for the Mongolian delegation incorporates imagery of the grasslands. For this Asian Games, 361 Degrees customized competition uniforms for six national and regional delegations and provided competition and training equipment for the Olympic Council of Asia Refugee Team. This is reportedly the fifth consecutive Asian Games that 361 Degrees has served, with more than 5.4 million pieces of sportswear supplied in total. Inside the gymnastics venue, a technical support team from Taishan Sports, a Chinese supplier of sports equipment and services based in east China's Shandong province, was carefully inspecting the equipment. Half a month before the opening, members of the team arrived in Japan in batches and began installing equipment at the competition, warm-up, and training venues. Athletes and coaches are familiar with their technical routines, but may not necessarily know the ins and outs of competition equipment. Taishan's specialists remain on-site throughout the Games to monitor performance and coordinate rapid responses. "Our protocols leave no room for deviation," noted Wang Wei, chief engineer of the support team. "We conduct a full systems check exactly one hour before every session -- a non-negotiable standard." Photo shows the venue for gymnastics competitions of the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026. (Photo courtesy of Taishan Sports) In addition to gymnastics, Taishan Sports is providing complete sets of competition equipment and one-stop event support for 16 sports at these Asian Games, including wushu, wrestling, and cycling. Since equipping the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, the company has maintained an unblemished record: zero malfunctions, zero safety incidents, and zero formal complaints. "From products to services and standards, and from elite competition venues to the mass market, we have always forged ahead with the mindset of climbers, reaching for greater heights," Wang said. "We aim to see Chinese sports brands shine even more brightly on the world stage." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Culture-infused tourism gains traction during National Day holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Culture-infused tourism gains traction during National Day holiday Tourists pose for a photo at the Hetou Old Street scenic area in Fengnan District of Tangshan City, north China's Hebei Province, Oct. 3, 2026. (Photo by Li Xiuqing/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- On the morning of Oct. 1, the first day of China's National Day holiday, the Confucius cruise ship slowly pulled away from a port in Jining, east China's Shandong Province, setting off for Nanyang ancient town on the city's southern outskirts. Named after the famous ancient Chinese philosopher Confucius, the ship was bound for a 2-hour-plus journey, passing stretches of the Grand Canal, the world's oldest artificial waterway system, which connects rivers in northern and eastern China and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2014. "We chose the cruise after seeing online that it offered a rich cultural experience," said Zhao Xiaojie from the provincial capital Jinan, as she and her 11-year-old son read the ancient texts on the cabin's decorations inspired by the Six Arts -- the six foundational disciplines of ancient Confucian education. Her choice reflects a broader trend during this year's National Day holiday, as cultural content is weighing more and more heavily in China's tourism products. NATIONAL DAY EXTRAVAGANZA "Cruises have operated on the same route before, but the Confucius incorporates many cultural elements and intangible cultural heritage experiences, turning it into a moving showcase of Confucianism on the Grand Canal," said Zhang Feng, head of the cruise route. The round-trip ticket includes shuttle services to scenic spots and admission to the Kangqian Bieyuan and Huji Qianzhuang attractions. Visitors can also watch a traditional fishermen's wedding ceremony and cormorant fishing performances in Nanyang ancient town, Zhang said. Such packages bring together Confucianism and the culture of the Grand Canal, he added. The unusual holiday calendar this year, with the Mid-Autumn Festival falling just three working days before the National Day holiday, has given fresh momentum to the integration of culture and tourism. Data from Chinese online travel platform Ctrip showed that one in 10 travelers chose to combine the two holidays by taking three days off to create a 13-day break. Nearly half of those taking an extended break traveled for more than eight days. The longer holidays have expanded the travel radius of Chinese tourists, bringing cultural and tourism products in more remote and lesser-known destinations into the spotlight. In Cangyuan Wa Autonomous County, southwest China's Yunnan Province, for example, tourists gathered at a square to pound freshly harvested rice and prepare new rice, filling the air with its aroma. "New rice festival activities and service facilities have been upgraded this year, allowing visitors to experience the authentic culture of the Wa ethnic group," said Li Lei, deputy general manager of the Cangyuan County Tourism Investment Company. Traditional culture is not the only draw. A growing number of travelers are also visiting landmarks associated with China's revolutionary history, driven in part by the patriotic sentiment associated with the National Day holiday. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. In Yudu County, east China's Jiangxi Province, the Memorial Park of the Starting Point of the Central Red Army's Long March has attracted large numbers of study-tour groups and is expected to receive nearly 300,000 visits during the seven-day holiday. Dai Bin, president of the China Tourism Academy, said the flow of visitors to revolutionary landmarks reflects people's emotional identification with the revolutionary traditions. When they travel, they don't just want to see history; they also want to draw deeper inspiration from the revolutionary legacy for their lives today, according to him. INNOVATION REMAINS KEY The trend has also fallen in line with a series of development plans China released recently. The 15th Five-Year Plan for culture and tourism development, released by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in September, calls for deeper integration between culture and tourism and their mutually reinforcing development with other areas of the economy and society. It stresses supporting the development of distinctive cultural industries and tourism in former revolutionary base areas. Moreover, it calls for expanding the space for cultural and tourism development, with deeper integration moving from resource consolidation and product integration toward new business models and broader applications. Hong'an Township in Xiushan Tujia and Miao Autonomous County, southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, has put such innovation into practice, drawing 190,000 tourist visits in the first two days of the holiday. Leveraging the cultural appeal of Border Town, a novel by renowned Chinese writer Shen Congwen, as well as its unique location where three provincial-level regions meet, the township has developed immersive, scenario-based tourism offerings that combine folk experiences, local cuisine and the nighttime economy. In Shandong, seven cities have joined forces to combine seven popular online-literature IPs with the region's landscapes and historical sites, encouraging fans to turn fictional worlds into real-life travel destinations. The model uses storytelling familiar to Generation Z to breathe new life into traditional cultural and tourism resources, converting online popularity into real-world tourism consumption. "The route runs from west to east, so fans can take a high-speed train and visit a different 'chapter' every day, which is very convenient," said Liu Wei, a fan of online literature born in the 2000s. For industry insiders, such efforts to generate more immersive cultural tourist activities are also necessary. Wu Liyun, a professor at Beijing International Studies University, said scenic spots once relied mainly on ticket sales, which is often unsustainable today. "The core of the industry transformation lies in adding more experiential offerings and opportunities for secondary consumption, with the focus on everyday settings, local culture and lifestyle-oriented services," she said. GLOBAL DRAW The shift has appealed to inbound travelers as well. With China offering unilateral visa-free entry to citizens of 50 countries and full mutual visa exemptions with 29 countries, its tourism industry has also been working to offer overseas tourists a wider range of immersive trips centered on cultural experiences. In Jingdezhen, east China's Jiangxi Province, where the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in July, growing numbers of overseas visitors are exploring historic sites, taking part in art workshops and browsing handicraft markets, while enjoying distinctive cafes and homestays. The city, known as the "Porcelain Capital," now offers a range of experiences for visitors seeking to explore its centuries-old ceramic traditions, according to Zhang Chen, a local tourism industry insider. Options include a one-day program combining an introduction to local ceramic culture with hands-on pottery making, or a three-day workshop led by inheritors of intangible cultural heritage. "Many overseas visitors now seek a deeper cultural connection, rather than simply sightseeing," Zhang said. In Beijing, veteran tourist guide Dou Junjie feels a similar trend. He provides guided bicycle tours along the Beijing Central Axis, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2024 that covers former imperial palaces and sacrificial structures. "More overseas visitors to Beijing would like to experience local life and learn about local culture," Dou said. According to Gao Zhengyang, a guest researcher with Jiangsu Su Merchants Bank, immersive travel across destinations is replacing sightseeing and photo stops, a wider range of trendy Chinese products is making its way onto tourists' shopping lists, and the mix of visitors is becoming more diverse. Gao said all of these trends point to improvements in the quality of "China Travel." Data from Ctrip shows that bookings for one-day tours by inbound tourists during this year's National Day holiday and the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday surged by over 400 percent year on year, with scenic spot ticket sales up more than 220 percent and train tickets more than 170 percent. Li Xinjian, a professor at the Beijing International Studies University, said the growth in inbound tourism during what is traditionally a peak season for domestic travel reflects the increasingly diverse experiences on offer. "Overseas tourists are finding that China offers not only beautiful scenery but also engaging cultural experiences," he said. For Wu Liyun, value-added services such as the cultural experiences in Jingdezhen and Beijing are particularly important, as they are far more appealing than standardized products and usually leave a much deeper impression on travelers. Wu believes Jingdezhen's model can be replicated in terms of how cultural content is presented. She cited her hometown of Linyi in Shandong Province, where willow weaving products are widely exported, and tourists can try their hand at the traditional craft and take their own creations home. "Every city has its own ways of life passed down through generations," she said. "What you are accustomed to in the place where you live can be incredibly fresh and novel to outsiders." item.title: China's railways see holiday return peak amid vibrant tourism market
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
China's railways see holiday return peak amid vibrant tourism market Passengers are seen at the waiting hall of Tianjin Railway Station in north China's Tianjin, Oct. 7, 2026. As the National Day holiday is drawing to a close, return travel flows increase across the country. (Photo by Du Penghui/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- China's railways saw the peak of the holiday return rush on Wednesday, with 24.15 million passenger trips expected on the final day of the National Day holiday, amid strong travel demand and vibrant tourism activity across the country. A total of 2,449 additional passenger trains were scheduled on Wednesday to cope with the surge in demand, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. On Tuesday, the country's railways handled 21.6 million passenger trips, marking the third consecutive day with more than 20 million journeys. Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Xi'an, Wuhan, Hangzhou, Chongqing and Shanghai were among the busiest cities for departures and arrivals, while passenger flows were particularly heavy on routes including Beijing-Shanghai, Wuhan-Shanghai, Wuhan-Shenzhen and Xi'an-Chengdu. Railway authorities across the country added services and expanded overnight operations to facilitate the return rush as China's tourism market remained vibrant during the seven-day holiday, with county-level destinations and nighttime consumption emerging as notable trends. County-level destinations gained popularity as travelers increasingly sought slower-paced and more immersive experiences away from major cities. From the coastal county of Lingshui in south China's Hainan Province to Mohe, a county-level city on the country's northern frontier, smaller destinations are drawing visitors with distinctive local experiences. Meanwhile, nighttime consumption flourished in many cities, with cultural performances, night markets, light shows and food fairs extending visitor stays and enriching holiday experiences. item.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026 opens with strong Chinese presence
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Frankfurt Book Fair 2026 opens with strong Chinese presence Visitors are seen at the Chinese joint exhibition booth of the Frankfurt Book Fair in Frankfurt, Germany, Oct. 7, 2026. The world's largest book fair opened Wednesday in Frankfurt, Germany, bringing together more than 4,000 publishing institutions from over 100 countries and regions. The Chinese joint exhibition booth covers 336 square meters and features more than 3,000 titles and over 4,600 copies of selected books. It combines book displays, rights negotiations, cultural exchanges and interactive experiences. (Xinhua/Du Zheyu) FRANKFURT, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- The world's largest book fair opened Wednesday in Frankfurt, Germany, bringing together more than 4,000 publishing institutions from over 100 countries and regions. Over 230,000 visitors are expected to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair, which runs until Sunday at Messe Frankfurt exhibition center. According to organizers, this year's fair emphasizes international crises and conflicts, the application and regulation of artificial intelligence (AI), rights trading, children's and young adult literature as well as audiobooks. A wide range of lectures, forums, performances, book signings and readings will also be held to promote exchanges within the publishing industry, while giving readers opportunities to interact directly with authors, publishers and media professionals. The Frankfurt Book Fair is also one of the most important international platforms for promoting Chinese publications and copyright exports. The Chinese joint exhibition booth covers 336 square meters and features more than 3,000 titles and over 4,600 copies of selected books. It combines book displays, rights negotiations, cultural exchanges and interactive experiences. During the fair, Chinese publishing and cultural institutions will organize 55 events, including thematic seminars, dialogues with authors, copyright signing ceremonies and new book launches. Founded in 1949, the Frankfurt Book Fair has been one of the world's largest publishing industry events. item.title: Small counties, big appeal: China's "golden week" fuels diverse getaways
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Small counties, big appeal: China's "golden week" fuels diverse getaways BEIJING, Oct. 7 (Xinhua) -- While tourism in China has traditionally been associated with breathtaking landscapes and photo opportunities, Wang Xin (pseudonym) opted for a different kind of National Day holiday this year: watching tennis. Well before the vacation she had purchased tickets for the Jingshan Tennis Open in central China's Hubei Province. A resident of Dongguan in Guangdong Province, about 1,000 kilometers away, she first learned about Jingshan because of the tournament. "I want to watch matches featuring several young WTA (Women's Tennis Association) and ATP (Association of Tennis Professionals) players up close," said the tennis enthusiast. She planned to spend three days watching the matches and the remaining four days exploring the county-level city, taking in its scenic mountains, valleys, and forests. During this National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7, one of China's few annual "golden weeks," authorities had projected 2.13 billion cross-regional passenger trips, averaging 300 million a day. People enjoy a match during the Jingshan Tennis Open in Jingshan, central China's Hubei Province, Oct. 4, 2026. (Photo by Lei Yixin/Xinhua) Data from Meituan, a major services platform, showed homestay bookings for four-to-six-night stays during the holiday rose 24 percent year on year as of Sept. 28, with county-level destinations posting particularly strong growth. Cultural and tourism authorities nationwide have introduced a range of creative initiatives to attract visitors, drawing on sports events, cultural IPs, ethnic traditions and distinctive natural landscapes. DESTINATIONS FOR DIVERSE DEMANDS Jingshan, a county-level city where tennis has been developing for more than 40 years, is known as China's "hometown of tennis." To boost tourism during the National Day holiday, local authorities announced that during the tournament period, a match ticket would entitle holders to discounts at over 100 local businesses. Merchants have also benefited from the holiday travel surge. Zuo Meng, a vendor selling knitted products, said she follows the local tennis events closely. "In Jingshan, there are tennis matches almost every week," she said, adding that a tournament can generate 6,000 to 7,000 yuan (about 895 to 1,044 U.S. dollars) in sales. Over the past two years, she has also taught knitting skills to more than 200 women so they, too, could benefit from tourism. Peng Jufang runs a farm in Wenfeng Village. Noticing tourists' enthusiasm for tennis, he founded his own tennis club in October last year. With more than 16 people coming each day to try their hand at tennis, he was kept busy during this National Day holiday, teaching visitors for over six hours a day. In 2025, Jingshan hosted 48 domestic and international sports events. The comprehensive output value of its "tennis plus" economy surpassed 3.5 billion yuan, drawing 3.52 million visits for matches and tourism. While Wang Xin enjoys tennis matches in Jingshan, cultural enthusiasts have meccas of their own to visit. Wang Yinan, in her 20s, traveled from Beijing to Ruicheng County in north China's Shanxi Province after watching the popular animation "All Wishes Come True." Hometown of the legendary figure behind the film's main protagonist, Lyu Dongbin, Ruicheng is home to the Yongle Palace, which is known for its celebrated murals. "It is such an exciting trip, and it's incredible to be in Lyu's hometown," said Wang, as she browsed creative products at the Yongle Palace store. Visitors are seen during a study tour for mural copying at the Yongle Palace scenic area in Ruicheng, north China's Shanxi Province, Oct. 2, 2026. (Photo by Guo Song/Xinhua) Liu Haibo, chairman of the Yongle Cultural Tourism Investment and Construction Co., Ltd., said the scenic site rolled out customized services to sustain its tourism growth following its viral popularity. Visitors can take photos in dedicated photo zones, guides explain the murals by linking them to scenes from the film, and tourists can attend interactive classes to learn mural copying and line drawing. The movie has helped raise the profile of Ruicheng, making it a sought-after destination, especially among young people. Statistics showed that between Oct. 1 and 5, Yongle Palace received about 80,000 visits, up more than 50 percent year on year. The ancient township of Fenghuang in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, central China's Hunan Province, has kept its tourist momentum following the Sept. 25-27 Mid-Autumn Festival holiday. During the National Day holiday, some visitors seeking to avoid the crowds have ventured beyond the ancient town of Fenghuang into surrounding mountains and villages, exploring rich ethnic cultures, such as Miao welcoming rituals, lantern shows and folk performances. INTERNATIONAL VISITORS JOINING THE RUSH The diverse tourism resources in China's counties are also luring international visitors away from metropolises like Beijing and Shanghai and toward niche attractions. Lucas Martin, 28, from France, visited Fenghuang for the first time after touring major Chinese cities. "Fenghuang feels entirely different from big cities," he said. "You can slow down here. You can admire the distinctive stilt houses lining the Tuojiang River and observe local residents in their daily lives." The in-depth county exploration impressed him with the town's authentic living vibe. "This is not merely a tourist attraction. Walking along the river and pausing at street corners makes me feel more than just a passing sightseer." Foreign tourists try specialty food of the Miao ethnic group at the ancient township of Fenghuang in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, central China's Hunan Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Hu Cong/Xinhua) Emma Wilson, an Australian traveler who is exploring small towns and countryside across China, tried on Miao ceremonial costumes in Fenghuang. "It is magical to walk into the old streets, dressed like locals," she said. Shop staff carefully helped her get fitted in the ethnic costume. "A simple landscape photo fades quickly from memory. But putting on traditional clothing, tasting local food and learning the stories behind folk customs create experiences that stay with you far longer," she said. Since December 2023, when China launched a trial policy granting unilateral visa exemptions to visitors from six countries, it has expanded unilateral visa-free entry to travelers from 50 countries as of September, allowing eligible visitors to stay for up to 30 days. In a separate move, authorities extended the visa-free transit period for certain countries from 72 or 144 hours to 240 hours in December 2024. So far the number of eligible countries has increased to 57. Official data revealed that foreign nationals made nearly 61.29 million border crossings in the first eight months of 2026, up 19.5 percent year on year, while one of the leading mobile payment platforms, Weixin Pay, reported that both the value and number of e-wallet transactions made by overseas users rose by more than 80 percent during the same period. On Sept. 24, China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism announced plans to develop more travel experiences that combine traditional culture with modern life during 2026-2030, aimed at helping foreign visitors travel more conveniently, enjoy more comfortable stays and gain a closer view of contemporary China. A National Day gala is held on the Tuojiang River at the ancient township of Fenghuang in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, central China's Hunan Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Hu Cong/Xinhua) FROM "CITY WALK" TO "COUNTRY WALK" Yang Han, a researcher at an institute affiliated to the travel platform Qunar, believes that county-level tourism began to accelerate around 2023-2024, as travelers increasingly sought destinations with fewer crowds, a lively atmosphere, opportunities for relaxation and immersive local experiences, as well as greater value for money. For instance, in Ruicheng of Shanxi, a set meal for one person may cost less than 20 yuan, the price of a cup of bubble tea in Beijing. Tuo Yanzheng, a professor at the College of Tourism and Service Management, Nankai University, said county areas hold rich agricultural, ecological and cultural resources with untapped consumption potential. "The key lies in turning these resource strengths into distinctive tourism products and consumption scenarios," she said. "It can not only meet people's increasingly diverse consumption demands, but also inject new vitality into the county economy." According to Sun Jiashan, a researcher at the Central Institute of Socialism, China's tourism market has evolved from "City Walk" to "Country Walk." Steadily improving transportation has made county-level destinations more accessible. By the end of 2025, China's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail. Shortly before the National Day holiday, the country opened four major high-speed railway sections, improving transport links across several regions and making travel easier for residents. The high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, with eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. In addition, Sun noted that beyond scenic spots, historical sites and natural landscapes, tourists are increasingly drawn to vibrant scenes of everyday life, such as farmers' markets and bustling streets. "This shift also places higher demands on local cultural and tourism infrastructure and services," he said. "As overseas tourists venture beyond first-tier cities into central and western regions and county-level areas, they encounter not only the outward face of China's development but also the texture of everyday social life," he said. "This helps break through cognitive filters and information barriers in Western societies and presents a real China to the world." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
